source_quotes: we work on a graph based chunkable system where we can switch models anytime, work with any models, any context size
so when it comes to chunking all remember we don't set limits at all, we work by model size
overlap_check: method_38 (30038) is about not adding caps to slow loops before measuring; this one is about content size, windows and refusal. Different trigger, cross-reference only.

payload.name: Chunk to the Reading Model's Window
payload.description: Content of any size is chunked to the window of the model that reads it. Nothing is capped, truncated or refused by size; the only bounds are named host-memory guards.

principles.name: The system is chunkable and model agnostic
principles.description: Any model and any context size can be used; a size is a reason to chunk, never a reason to stop.

principles.name: A response is data
principles.description: What a model produces is stored and graphed whole; previews are for logs only.

heuristics.condition: code contains a numeric cut such as take(N), a fixed byte length or a fixed item count on content
heuristics.action: find what the cut protects and replace it with chunking by the reading model's window, or record why it is a host guard

heuristics.condition: a summary says a prompt was 'too long'
heuristics.action: check whether it was chunked; a prompt may be as long as the content needs

decision_rules.name: Chunk instead of cutting
decision_rules.condition: input, context or output is larger than the reading model's window
decision_rules.outcome: split it into chunks sized to that model's window and process each chunk (or send numbered parts whole); never cut the content or return an error because of its size

decision_rules.name: Work by the model's size
decision_rules.condition: the model that reads or writes changes
decision_rules.outcome: size the chunks and windows from the model now in use and keep any derived data keyed by model size so a return to that size reuses it

decision_rules.name: Never truncate stored text
decision_rules.condition: a text is stored, graphed or handed to another stage
decision_rules.outcome: store the whole text; shorten only inside log previews, and say so in the log line

decision_rules.name: Do not cap a response
decision_rules.condition: a call to a model is built
decision_rules.outcome: send no maximum token value to the provider; a caller's length is a hint to the model about the answer's shape, and a local runtime may use half its window as a physical limit

decision_rules.name: Name a host guard honestly
decision_rules.condition: a bound is unavoidable because of host memory or transport
decision_rules.outcome: make it an explicit tunable guard, reply with a clear error that says it is a host guard, and describe it as a guard, not as a limit of the system
